thread:
jia: Quick question for the ruby maintainers  I bumped oauth2-client to 1.8.2 in the sampleapp to get past a TLS flake in CI. Local onboarding now flakes with a 401 right after a token refresh. Anyone seen this pattern?

noah: Repro steps I used:
1) RAILS_ENV=development bundle exec rake sample:onboard
2) Trigger refresh (POST /refresh_token)
3) Immediately call /profile -> sometimes 401, then 200 on retry
Logs show refresh returned access_token but header sent had a trailing newline in a few runs.

rebecca: That sounds like the helper method that writes the token file changed. Did you inspect the file on disk when it fails?

jia: Yup. Grabbed the token file from a failing run: "eyJ...\n" (ends with newline). When we build header we do `Authorization: Bearer #{token}` which includes the newline. Some HTTP parsers treat that as malformed and return 401.

noah: Minimal curl test: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJ...\n" http://localhost:4000/profile` -> 401; without newline -> 200. Intermittent because the helper sometimes writes with a trailing newline.

rebecca: Two easy options: sanitize in sampleapp (token = token.to_s.strip) or pin oauth2-client to previous patch. I'd add a small regression spec that simulates token file with trailing whitespace.

jia: I'll add the .strip fix + an integration spec that writes a token file with newline and asserts outgoing header has no newline. I'll also add a note in the PR linking to an upstream issue if we confirm it's a gem regression.

ci-bot: CI queued: ruby-sampleapp-smoke #601.

noah: Thanks  with the test we can keep the bump. If upstream changes behavior again we can pin in the short term.
